Finally, some epistemologists reject both Reductionism and Non-Reductionism in favor of various hybrid views.

Or, one might opt for a hybrid view according to which the hearer and the speaker both have an important role to play in the hearer’s ability to acquire testimonial justification, i.e., it takes two to tango, so to speak.
The hope here is that by requiring contributions from both the speaker and the hearer, all of the worries associated with standard versions of Reductionism and Non-reductionism can be avoided.
